rules.title: Algorithmic Rent-Setting Software Ban
rules.requirement: Landlords and rental housing providers in Santa Ana are prohibited from selling, licensing, or using algorithmic rent-setting software that relies on nonpublic competitor data (like real-time rents, lease renewals, and occupancy) to set rental prices.
rules.key_value: Ban on algorithmic devices; up to $1,000 civil penalty per violation
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to residential rental property within Santa Ana city limits; does not apply to software relying solely on publicly available or aggregate historical data, or tools used to comply with affordable housing program requirements.
rules.exemptions: Pricing software that relies solely on publicly available data, aggregate historical data, or tools used to comply with affordable housing program requirements.
rules.penalty: Civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, plus injunctive relief, damages, and attorney's fees; landlords caught using banned software could be fined $1,000.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Mun. Code (Algorithmic Rent-Setting Ordinance, 2026)
rules.quoted_span: The ordinance, approved on Tuesday, Feb. 17, for a first reading and set for a final vote on March 3, prohibits the sale, licensing, provision and use of certain algorithmic rent-setting software for residential rental properties.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the software relies solely on publicly available or aggregate historical data, or is used for affordable housing compliance

rules.conflict_note: Secondary sources differ slightly on exact effective date: one source implies the ordinance took effect upon final vote (March 3, 2026), another (OCBJ) is dated March 9, 2026 describing 'Tuesday's vote' as final; exact effective date not independently confirmed by official text.
